audit.summary: An impossible natural map from the completed cone to the specified p-adically completed graded absolute integral closure leaves the global geometric application without its stated proof. A separate exact normalized-length calculation corrects two auxiliary constants while preserving the qualitative conclusions. No counterexample to a theorem is claimed.

proposition.claim:
Let \((R,\mathfrak m,k)\) be a complete Noetherian local domain of mixed characteristic \((0,p)\), dimension \(d\), with perfect residue field. The paper fixes a finite coefficient-ring inclusion \[A=W(k)\mathopen{[\![}x_2,\ldots,x_d\mathclose{]\!]}\subset R,
 \qquad
 A_n=A[p^{1/p^n},x_2^{1/p^n},\ldots,x_d^{1/p^n}],\] and its \(p\)-adically completed tower \(A_\infty\). Normalized length on a finite-level module is scaled by \(p^{-nd}\). The relevant algebra is \(B=(R\otimes_A A_\infty)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\), not its image in a chosen absolute integral closure. For an \(\mathfrak m\)-primary ideal \(J\) and the non-splitting ideal \(I_\infty\subset B\), the invariants are \[e_{\mathrm{perfd}}^{\underline{x}}(J)=\lambda_\infty(B/JB),
 \qquad
 s_{\mathrm{perfd}}^{\underline{x}}(R)=\lambda_\infty(B/I_\infty).\] Their dependence on the chosen tower is retained throughout. Parameter independence is posed as Conjecture 8.1, not established by this paper. In particular, the class-group bound in Theorem 7.0.12 uses some choices of parameters; it must not be read as proving independence for arbitrary choices.

The regularity checks reconstructed the chain from the rank/multiplicity comparison and parameter limit closure to \(e_{\mathrm{perfd}}^{\underline{x}}(R)\geq1\), the equality criterion, and the implication \(s_{\mathrm{perfd}}^{\underline{x}}(R)=1\Rightarrow R\) regular. The final regularity argument relies on the cited homological criterion; its external proof was not re-audited. The distinction between \(B\) and its image is essential even for ramified regular rings and is correctly emphasized in the source.

For positive signature, the converse implication is quantified as \[\forall\,0\ne g\in R,\quad \exists e,\quad
 \forall\,\text{perfectoid BCM }R^+\text{-algebras }C:
 \quad R\xrightarrow{\,1\mapsto g^{1/p^e}\,}C
 \text{ is pure}.\] The exponent can depend on \(g\); it is not one exponent for all \(g\). The domination lemma and essential socle of the injective hull support uniformity over \(C\). The forward implication from BCM-regular pairs retains the effective boundary and log-\(\mathbb Q\)-Cartier assumptions. For rational signature, the stabilized tail-span argument in Theorem 5.4.10 supplies a positive valuation threshold uniform over all socle injections. Pointwise positivity alone would not justify the infimum. Problem 2 changes its numerical lower bound, not that uniformity.

Theorem 7.0.4 concerns a normal integral scheme \(Y\), projective over \(R=H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\), with equidimensional fibers. Here \(R\) is a complete Noetherian local domain with algebraically closed residue field. An effective \(\mathbb Q\)-divisor \(\Delta\) satisfies \(-(K_Y+\Delta)\) ample, and for every effective Cartier divisor \(D>0\) there is \(\epsilon>0\) such that \((Y,\Delta+\epsilon D)\) is globally \(+\)-regular. The conclusion is finiteness of the étale fundamental group of every open subset with complement of codimension at least two.

Equation reference: eq:badmap. In the proof, the chosen section ring \(S'\) is finite over \[A''=A'[x_0,\ldots,x_r],\qquad
 A'=W(k)\mathopen{[\![}y_1,\ldots,y_s\mathclose{]\!]}.\] Write \(\mathfrak n\) for its homogeneous maximal ideal and \(S=\widehat{S'}_{\mathfrak n}\). Claim 7.0.5 asserts BCM-regularity of \((S,\Delta_S)\) and hence positive perfectoid signature. After another graded finite extension and completion \(S_1\), the proof asserts a natural factorization \[
 S\longrightarrow S_1\longrightarrow
 T:=\widehat{S'^{+,\mathrm{GR}}}^{\,p}.\] It explicitly defines the last completion as \(p\)-adic. This factorization supplies the tensor product and local-cohomology map used to invoke Proposition 5.2.3. The subsequent reduction of covers of \(Y\) to covers of \(S\) needs the resulting positive signature.

The section ring S' is finite graded over A''=W(k)[[y_1,...,y_s]][x_0,...,x_r]. C=S'^{+,GR} is integral over S' under its stated definition. x_0 is in the homogeneous maximal ideal used to complete S'. The asserted natural map is a unital S'-algebra map. The geometric application retains normality, completeness, algebraically closed residue field, equidimensional fibers, log-Fano ampleness and global +-regularity for sufficiently small positive boundaries.

Definition 4.0.11, p. 31, extends the \(\mathfrak m_A\)-adic order to the tower by total monomial degree, with \(v(p)=v(x_i)=1\). For \(\epsilon>0\), the lemma sets \(I_n=\{a\in A_n:v(a)\geq\epsilon\}\) and uses \[\operatorname{length}_A(A_n/I_n)\geq p^{nd}\epsilon^d.\] At the end of Theorem 5.4.11, the paper instead calculates \(\lambda_\infty(A_\infty/\{v\geq p^{-e_0}\})=p^{-e_0}\). Both quantities must respect the dimension-\(d\) normalization.

A=W(k)[[x_2,...,x_d]], regular mixed characteristic with perfect residue field. A_n adjoins p^n-th roots of all d regular parameters. The stated valuation is total monomial degree, with v(p)=v(x_i)=1. Normalized length scales finite-level A-length by p^(-nd).
